title: Biodiversity Risk
venue: Review of Finance (2026), 30(1): 131–161 (Special Issue for Biodiversity and Natural Resource Finance)
abstract: We explore the effects of physical and regulatory risks related to biodiversity loss on economic activity and asset values. We first develop a news-based measure of aggregate biodiversity risk and analyze how it varies over time. We also construct and publicly release several firm-level measures of exposure to biodiversity risk, based on textual analyses of firms' 10-K statements, the holdings of biodiversity-related funds, and a large survey of finance professionals, regulators, and academics. Exposures to biodiversity risk vary substantially across industries in a way that is economically sensible and distinct from exposures to climate risk. We find evidence that biodiversity risks already affect equity prices: returns of portfolios that are sorted on our measures of biodiversity risk exposure covary positively with innovations in aggregate biodiversity risk. However, our survey indicates that market participants do not perceive the current pricing of biodiversity risks in equity markets to be adequate. We also construct several measures of biodiversity risk exposure across U.S. counties, but find little evidence that those exposures are priced in municipal bond markets.
abstract_zh: 我们探讨了与生物多样性丧失相关的物理风险和监管风险对经济活动和资产价值的影响。我们首先构建了一个基于新闻的总体生物多样性风险指标，并分析其随时间的变化。我们还基于对企业10-K报告的文本分析、生物多样性相关基金的持仓，以及对金融从业者、监管机构和学者的大型调查，构建并公开发布了多项企业层面的生物多样性风险暴露指标。生物多样性风险暴露在不同行业之间存在显著差异，且这种差异在经济上是合理的，并且有别于气候风险暴露。我们发现有证据表明，生物多样性风险已经影响股票价格：按照我们的生物多样性风险暴露指标分类构建的投资组合收益，与总体生物多样性风险的新息呈正相关。然而，我们的调查显示，市场参与者并不认为股票市场目前对生物多样性风险的定价是充分的。我们还构建了美国各县生物多样性风险暴露的若干指标，但几乎没有证据表明这些暴露在市政债券市场中得到了定价。

title: A Quantity-Based Approach to Constructing Climate Risk Hedge Portfolios
abstract: We propose a new methodology to build portfolios that hedge the economic and financial risks from climate change. Our quantity-based approach exploits information on how mutual fund managers trade in response to idiosyncratic changes in their climate risk beliefs. We exploit two types of idiosyncratic belief shocks: (i) instances when fund advisers experience local extreme heat events that are known to shift climate change beliefs, and (ii) instances when fund managers change the language in shareholder disclosures to express concerns about climate risks. We use the funds' observed portfolio changes around such idiosyncratic belief shocks to predict how investors will reallocate their capital in response to aggregate climate news shocks that shift the beliefs and asset demands of many investors and thus move equilibrium prices. We show that a portfolio that is long stocks that investors tend to buy after experiencing negative idiosyncratic climate belief shocks, and short stocks that investors tend to sell, appreciates in value in periods with negative aggregate climate news shocks. Our quantity-based portfolios have superior out-ofsample hedge performance compared to portfolios constructed using existing alternative methods. The key advantage of the quantity-based approach is that it learns from rich cross-sectional trading responses rather than time-series price information, which is particularly limited in the case of newly emerging risks such as those from climate change. We also demonstrate the versatility of the quantity-based approach by constructing successful hedge portfolios for aggregate unemployment and house price risk.
abstract_zh: 我们提出了一种构建投资组合的新方法，用以对冲气候变化带来的经济与金融风险。我们基于数量的方法，利用了共同基金经理在其气候风险信念发生特质性变化时如何交易的信息。我们利用两类特质性信念冲击：（i）基金顾问经历已知会改变气候变化信念的当地极端高温事件的情形；（ii）基金经理在股东披露文件中改变措辞、表达对气候风险关切的情形。我们利用基金在此类特质性信念冲击前后观察到的投资组合变化，预测投资者在面对总体气候新闻冲击时将如何重新配置其资本——这些总体冲击会改变众多投资者的信念和资产需求，从而使均衡价格发生变动。我们表明，做多那些投资者在经历负向特质性气候信念冲击后倾向于买入的股票、做空那些投资者倾向于卖出的股票，所构建的投资组合在出现负向总体气候新闻冲击的时期会升值。与采用现有其他替代方法构建的投资组合相比，我们基于数量的投资组合具有更优越的样本外对冲表现。基于数量方法的关键优势在于，它从丰富的横截面交易反应中学习，而非依赖时间序列价格信息——而后者在气候变化等新兴风险的情形下尤为有限。我们还通过构建针对总体失业和房价风险的有效对冲组合，展示了基于数量方法的通用性。

title: Investor Beliefs and Expectation Formation
venue: Annual Review of Financial Economics, forthcoming

title: Nature and Biodiversity Loss: A Research Agenda for Financial Economics
venue: Journal of Finance: Insights and Perspectives, forthcoming
abstract: We outline a research agenda to better understand the economic and financial consequences of nature and biodiversity loss. Our starting point is a simple model in which ecosystem services—such as pollination, water filtration, and carbon sequestration—enter economic production, and where nature degradation and climate change reinforce one another through a “Twin-Crises Multiplier.” We then extend this framework to allow for heterogeneity across firms, industries, and geographies in how they depend on, and in turn affect, nature. This broader perspective provides a foundation for empirical analyses of how biodiversity loss influences aggregate output, firm productivity, and financial risk. We conclude by identifying opportunities for asset pricing and corporate finance research to systematically incorporate nature and biodiversity into financial economics. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 我们提出一项研究议程，以更好地理解自然与生物多样性丧失的经济和金融后果。我们的出发点是一个简单模型，其中授粉、水净化和碳封存等生态系统服务进入经济生产，而自然退化与气候变化通过“双重危机乘数”相互强化。随后，我们扩展了该框架，允许企业、行业和地理区域在对自然的依赖程度及其反过来的影响方面存在异质性。这一更广阔的视角为实证分析生物多样性丧失如何影响总产出、企业生产率和金融风险奠定了基础。最后，我们指出了资产定价与公司金融研究的机会，以便系统地将自然与生物多样性纳入金融经济学之中。美国国家经济研究局（NBER）工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可在www.nber.org免费下载本文。

title: Prediction When Factors are Weak
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association, forthcoming

title: The Decline of the S&P 500 Variance Risk Premium
Climate Transition Risks and the Energy Sector
abstract: We build a general equilibrium model to study how climate transition risks affect energy prices and the valuations of different firms in the energy sector. We consider two types of fossil fuel firms: incumbents that have developed oil reserves they can extract today or tomorrow, and new entrants that must invest in exploration and drilling today to have reserves to potentially extract tomorrow. There are also renewable energy firms that produce emission-free energy but cannot currently serve non-electrifiable sectors of the economy. We analyze three sources of climate transition risk: (i) changes in the probability of a technological breakthrough that allows renewable energy firms to serve all economic sectors; (ii) changes in expected future taxes on carbon emissions; and (iii) restrictions on today's development of additional fossil fuel production capacity. We show that different transition risks—and, importantly, uncertainty about their realizations—have distinct effects on firms' decisions, on their valuations, and on equilibrium energy prices. We provide empirical support for the heterogeneous effects of different transition risks on energy prices and stock returns of firms in different energy sub-sectors. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 我们构建了一个一般均衡模型，以研究气候转型风险如何影响能源价格以及能源部门不同企业的估值。我们考虑两类化石燃料企业：一类是已开发出石油储量、可以在当前或未来开采的既有企业；另一类是新进入者，必须在当前投资勘探和钻井，才能在未来拥有可能开采的储量。此外还有可再生能源企业，它们生产零排放能源，但目前无法服务于无法电气化的经济部门。我们分析了三类气候转型风险来源：（i）使可再生能源企业能够服务于所有经济部门的技术突破概率的变化；（ii）未来碳排放税预期的变化；（iii）对当前新增化石燃料生产能力开发的限制。我们表明，不同的转型风险——更重要的是，关于其实际实现情况的不确定性——对企业决策、企业估值以及均衡能源价格具有不同的影响。我们为不同转型风险对能源价格以及能源各细分行业企业股票回报的异质性影响提供了实证支持。美国国家经济研究局（NBER）工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可在www.nber.org免费下载本文。

title: Learning and the Emergence of Nonlinearity in Financial Markets
abstract: Outside the knife-edge case of normally distributed priors, when agents are learning about a hidden state, the higher moments of their beliefs vary endogenously in response to observed signals. This paper formalizes that variation and shows that it is characterized by a simple recursion. Empirically, financial markets are a particularly useful laboratory for studying the model's predictions because high-frequency data is available along with well-developed methods for estimating higher moments. The predictions of a filtering model for the joint dynamics of the moments of beliefs fit well with a wide range of observed behaviors in financial markets, including, among others, the skewness of returns across frequencies and the volatility, skewness, and persistence of the return volatility process.

title: Using Density Forecasts to Measure the Stability of Inflation Expectations
abstract: The anchoring of inflation expectations is a major objective of modern monetary policy. Under very weak conditions, allowing for a wide range of deviations from rationality and from the usual linear-Gaussian structure, the local sensitivity of an agent's expectations to news is equal to their subjective uncertainty multiplied by the precision of the observed signal. Instrumental variables estimates show that uncertainty is a significant determinant of expectational anchoring for survey participants, and the data is consistent with the model's implication of proportionality – a hypothetical agent with zero uncertainty would ignore all signals. At the aggregate level, average uncertainty predicts the sensitivity of average expectations to realized inflation surprises, and with a magnitude consistent with the micro IV-based estimates. The results imply that as of 2025, household inflation expectations were 2–3 times more sensitive to news than prior to 2020.

title: Four Facts about ESG Beliefs and Investor Portfolios
Nature Loss and Climate Change: the Twin-Crises Multiplier
abstract: We study the economic effects of the interaction of nature loss and climate change in a model that incorporates important aspects of both processes. We capture the distinct ways in which they affect economic activity—with nature constituting a key factor of production and climate change destroying parts of output—but also the ways in which they interact: climate change causes nature loss, and nature provides both a carbon sink and adaptation tools to reduce climate damages. Our analysis of these feedback loops reveals a novel amplification channel—the Twin-Crises Multiplier—that systematically affects optimal climate and nature conservation policies. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 我们在一个纳入了两个过程重要方面的模型中，研究自然丧失与气候变化相互作用的经济效应。我们刻画了二者影响经济活动的不同方式——自然构成关键的生产要素，而气候变化则摧毁部分产出——同时也刻画了二者相互作用的方式：气候变化导致自然丧失，而自然既提供碳汇，又提供减少气候损害的适应工具。我们对这些反馈回路的分析揭示了一种新的放大渠道——“双重危机乘数”，它系统性地影响最优的气候与自然保护政策。美国国家经济研究局（NBER）工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可在www.nber.org免费下载本文。

title: Test Assets and Weak Factors
The Economics of Biodiversity Loss
abstract: We explore the economic effects of biodiversity loss by developing an ecologically-founded model that captures how different species interact to deliver the ecosystem services that complement other factors of economic production. Aggregate ecosystem services are produced by combining several non-substitutable ecosystem functions such as pollination and water filtration, which are each provided by many substitutable species playing similar roles. As a result, economic output is an increasing but highly concave function of species richness. The marginal economic value of a species depends on three factors: (i) the number of similar species within its ecosystem function, (ii) the marginal importance of the affected function for overall ecosystem productivity, and (iii) the extent to which ecosystem services constrain economic output in each country. Using our framework, we derive expressions for the fragility of ecosystem service provision and its evolution over time, which depends, among other things, on the distribution of biodiversity losses across ecosystem functions. We discuss how these fragility measures can help policymakers assess the risks induced by biodiversity loss and prioritize conservation efforts. We also embed our model of ecosystem service production in a standard economic model to study optimal land use when land use raises output at the cost of reducing biodiversity. We find that even in settings where species loss does not reduce output substantially today, it lowers growth opportunities and reduces resilience to future species loss, especially when past species loss has been asymmetric across functions. Consistent with these predictions of our model, we show empirically that news about biodiversity loss increases spreads on credit default swaps (CDS) more for countries with more depleted ecosystems.
abstract_zh: 我们通过构建一个以生态学为基础的模型，探讨生物多样性丧失的经济效应。该模型刻画了不同物种如何相互作用，以提供补充其他经济生产要素的生态系统服务。总体生态系统服务由若干不可替代的生态系统功能（如授粉和水净化）组合而成，而每一种功能又由许多发挥相似作用的、可相互替代的物种提供。因此，经济产出是物种丰富度的一个递增但高度凹的函数。一个物种的边际经济价值取决于三个因素：（i）其所属生态系统功能中相似物种的数量；（ii）受影响功能对整体生态系统生产力的边际重要性；（iii）生态系统服务在各国在多大程度上制约经济产出。利用我们的框架，我们推导出生态系统服务供给脆弱性及其随时间演变的表达式，这一脆弱性除其他因素外，还取决于生物多样性损失在各生态系统功能之间的分布。我们讨论了这些脆弱性指标如何帮助决策者评估生物多样性丧失所引发的风险，并排定保护工作的优先次序。我们还将生态系统服务生产模型嵌入一个标准经济模型中，以研究在土地利用以牺牲生物多样性为代价提高产出的情形下，最优土地利用应如何安排。我们发现，即使在物种丧失在当前并未显著降低产出的情形下，它也会降低增长机会，并削弱对未来物种丧失的抵御能力，尤其是当过去的物种丧失在各功能之间并不均衡时。与模型的这些预测相一致，我们实证地表明，关于生物多样性丧失的新闻会使生态系统退化更严重的国家的信用违约互换（CDS）利差上升得更多。

title: What Drives Booms and Busts in Value?
abstract: Value investing delivers volatile returns, with large drawdowns during both market booms and busts. This paper interprets these returns through an intertemporal CAPM, which predicts that aggregate cash flow, discount rate, and volatility news all move value returns. We document that indeed these shocks explain a large fraction of quarterly value returns over the last 60 years. We also distinguish between the intra-industry and inter-industry components of value, showing that the ICAPM explains the former better. Finally, we develop a novel methodology to perform this decomposition at the daily frequency, using it to interpret value returns during the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: Equity Term Structures without Dividend Strips Data
Recent Developments in Financial Risk and the Real Economy
Cross-Sectional Uncertainty and the Business Cycle: Evidence from 40 Years of Options Data
Factor Models, Machine Learning, and Asset Pricing
The Collateral Rule: Evidence from the Credit Default Swap Market
The Effect of Climate Risks on the Interactions between Financial Markets and Energy Companies
Asset Pricing with Omitted Factors
Climate Change and Long-Run Discount Rates: Evidence from Real Estate
abstract: We explore what private market data can tell us about the appropriate discount rates for valuing investments in climate change abatement. We estimate the term structure of discount rates for real estate up to the very long horizons relevant for investments in climate change abatement. The housing term structure is downward-sloping, reaching 2.6% at horizons beyond 100 years. We also show that real estate is exposed to both consumption risk and climate risk. We explore the implications of these new data using a tractable asset pricing model that incorporates important features of climate change. Climate change is modeled as a rare catastrophic event, the probability of which increases with economic growth. Economic activity partially mean reverts following a climate disaster, capturing the ability of the economy to adapt. As a result, short-run cash flows are more exposed to climate risk than long-run cash flows, allowing us to match the observed housing term structure. The model and data provide simple yet powerful guidance for appropriate discount rates for investments that hedge climate disaster risk. The term structure of these discount rates is upward-sloping but bounded above by the risk-free rate. For extremely far horizons at which we do not observe the risk-free rate, the estimated long-run discount rates for housing (a risky asset) provide an upper bound that becomes tighter with maturity. This suggests that the appropriate discount rates for investments in climate change abatement are low at all horizons, substantially below those conventionally used for valuing these investments and for determining the social cost of carbon.
abstract_zh: 我们探讨私人市场数据能够告诉我们，在为气候变化减缓投资估值时应采用何种适当的贴现率。我们估计了房地产的贴现率期限结构，其期限可延伸至与气候变化减缓投资相关的极长期限。住房的期限结构呈向下倾斜态势，在100年以上的期限处达到2.6%。我们还表明，房地产既面临消费风险，也面临气候风险。我们利用一个包含气候变化重要特征的易于处理的资产定价模型，探讨了这些新数据的含义。气候变化被建模为一种罕见的灾难性事件，其发生概率随经济增长而上升。经济活动在气候灾害之后会部分地向均值回归，这刻画了经济的适应能力。因此，短期现金流比长期现金流更多地暴露于气候风险，这使我们能够拟合观察到的住房期限结构。该模型与数据为对冲气候灾难风险的投资提供了简单而有力的贴现率指导。这些贴现率的期限结构呈向上倾斜态势，但以无风险利率为上限。对于我们无法观察到无风险利率的极远期限，住房（一种风险资产）所估计的长期贴现率提供了一个上界，且该上界随期限延长而收紧。这表明，用于气候变化减缓投资的适当贴现率在所有期限上都较低，显著低于传统上用于此类投资估值以及确定社会的碳成本时所使用的贴现率。

title: Climate Finance
abstract: Climate finance is the study of local and global financing of public and private investment that seeks to support mitigation of and adaptation to climate change. In 2017, the Review of Financial Studies launched a competition among scholars to develop research proposals on the topic with the goal of publishing this special volume. We describe the competition, how the nine projects featured in this volume came to be published, and frame their findings within what we view as a broader climate finance research program.
abstract_zh: 气候金融研究的是为支持减缓和适应气候变化而进行的公共与私人投资的地方和全球融资问题。2017年，《金融研究评论》（Review of Financial Studies）发起了一项面向学者的竞赛，征集关于该主题的研究提案，目标是出版本期特刊。我们介绍了这一竞赛，以及本特刊所收录的九个项目是如何产生并得以出版的，并将其研究发现置于我们认为更为广泛的气候金融研究计划之中加以阐释。

title: Five Facts About Beliefs and Portfolios
Hedging Macroeconomic and Financial Uncertainty and Volatility
The Joint Dynamics of Investor Beliefs and Trading during the COVID-19 Crash
Thousands of Alpha Tests
Hedging Climate Change News
abstract: We propose and implement a procedure to dynamically hedge climate change risk. To create our hedge target, we extract innovations in climate news series that we construct through textual analysis of high-dimensional data on newspaper coverage of climate change. We then use a mimicking-portfolio approach to build climate change hedge portfolios using a large panel of equity returns. We discipline the exercise by using third-party ESG scores of firms to model their climate risk exposures. We show that this approach yields parsimonious and industry-balanced portfolios that perform well in hedging innovations in climate news both in sample and out of sample. The resulting hedge portfolios outperform alternative hedging strategies based primarily on industry tilts. We discuss multiple directions for future research on financial approaches to managing climate risk.
abstract_zh: 我们提出并实施了一种动态对冲气候变化风险的程序。为构建对冲目标，我们从高维报纸气候变化报道数据的文本分析中构建的气候新闻序列中提取新息。随后，我们利用一大批股票回报面板，采用模仿组合（mimicking-portfolio）方法构建气候变化对冲组合。我们利用第三方提供的企业ESG评分来建模企业的气候风险暴露，以约束这一分析。我们表明，该方法所产生的投资组合简洁且行业均衡，无论是在样本内还是样本外，对气候新闻新息的对冲效果都表现良好。所得的对冲组合优于那些主要依赖行业倾斜的替代对冲策略。我们讨论了金融方法管理气候风险的多个未来研究方向。

title: Taming the Factor Zoo: a Test of New Factors
Uncertainty Shocks as Second-Moment News Shocks
An Intertemporal CAPM with Stochastic Volatility
Excess Volatility: Beyond Discount Rates
The Price of Variance Risk
A Review of Long-Run Discounting: Evidence from Housing Markets
Asset Pricing in the Frequency Domain: Theory and Empirics

Systemic Risk and the Macroeconomy: An Empirical Evaluation
Very Long-Run Discount Rates
No News is News: Do Markets Underreact to Nothing?
Credit Default Swap Spreads and Systemic Financial Risk
abstract: This paper measures the joint default risk of financial institutions by exploiting information about counterparty risk in credit default swaps (CDS). A CDS contract written by a bank to insure against the default of another bank is exposed to the risk that both banks default. From CDS spreads we can then learn about the joint default risk of pairs of banks. From bond prices we can learn the individual default probabilities. Since knowing individual and pairwise probabilities is not sufficient to fully characterize multiple default risk, I derive the tightest bounds on the probability that many banks fail simultaneously.

title: Hard Times
Intangible Capital, Relative Asset Shortages, and Bubbles
Forced Sales and House Prices
